args.sql:
SELECT service, SUM(unblended_cost) AS total_cost
FROM provision_cost
WHERE account_id = '604918372251'
  AND month_ts IN ('2026-09-01', '2026-10-01')
  AND usage_date >= '2026-09-14'
  AND usage_date < '2026-09-21'
GROUP BY service
ORDER BY total_cost DESC
LIMIT 20

SELECT p.babylon_guid, p.catalog_id, p.provisioned_at, p.retired_at
FROM provisions p
WHERE p.babylon_guid = 'mz4tq'
LIMIT 5

counts_missed.asked_by: how much did that service cost
counts_missed.rationale: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud - Compute's window cost, the largest item of the account's row. It carries 'which service accounts for most of it' too: there is no bare service-name fact, because EC2 is a guess any model makes for an AWS account (the 073 lesson). 1,148 occurs only as that item's cost
